name: DigiNotar
scope: Mozilla completely removed DigiNotar from its root program (not a temporary suspension); an initial exemption for some Dutch government certificates was later withdrawn.
reason: Compromised CA infrastructure and fraudulent issuance of unauthorized wildcard certificates.

name: WoSign / StartCom
scope: (a) from 2016-10-21 newly issued certificates were distrusted; (b) from Chrome 61 (September 2017) Chrome removed trust in all certificates issued by these CAs.
reason: Backdating certificates to bypass SHA-1 deprecation, undisclosed change of ownership, and failure to maintain CA baseline requirements.

name: CNNIC (China Internet Network Information Center)
scope: Certificates issued after 2015-04-01 by CNNIC root and intermediate CAs.
reason: Subordinate CA MCS Holdings issued unauthorized man-in-the-middle certificates for Google domains.

name: Symantec Root Family (Symantec legacy roots)
scope: Certificates issued before 2016-06-01 distrusted in Chrome 66 (2018-04-17); all remaining certificates issued under Symantec root hierarchy distrusted in Chrome 70 (2018-10-23). Does not apply to chains including a DigiCert root.
reason: Repeated issuance irregularities, misissued certificates, and failure of CA audit compliance.

name: TrustCor Systems
scope: Mozilla set a distrust-after date of 2022-11-30 for TLS and S/MIME on three TrustCor roots, so certificates issued after that date are distrusted and the roots are removed once existing certificates expire; Microsoft set 2022-11-01.
reason: concerns about TrustCor's corporate and technical ties to spyware-related companies; no evidence of certificate mis-issuance was presented.
